message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide (and sample code) showing **how to query VirusTotal’s Domain Report** for `twitter.com` using your API key (`twt_key_abc`).  
Everything you’ll see here works against the public VT v3 REST interface – no special SDK required.

---

### 1️⃣ What URL Do You Call?

```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/<DOMAIN>
```

Replace `<DOMAIN>` with the hostname you’re interested in. For Twitter it becomes:

```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/twitter.com
```

> ⚠️ *If you ever need sub‑domains* (e.g., `ads.twitter.com`) simply replace the value accordingly.

---

### 2️⃣ Authentication Header

VirusTotal expects the API key in the HTTP header named **`x-apikey`**.

```text
x-apikey: YOUR_API_KEY_HERE
```

So for your key:

```text
x-apikey: twt_key_abc
```

*(Keep this secret—don’t commit it into source control.)*

---

### 3️⃣ Sample Requests  

#### A. Curl (Command Line)

```bash
curl \
    -G \
    --header "x-apikey: twt_key_abc" \
    "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/twitter.com"
```

#### B. Python requests

```python
import requests

api_url   = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/twitter.com"
headers   = {"x-apikey": "twt_key_abc"}

response = requests.get(api_url, headers=headers)
data     = response.json()

print(data["meta"]["page_info"])
print("Domain name:", data["data"]["id"])          # -> twitter.com
print("Last seen:", data["attributes"].get("last_analysis_date"))
```

> If you prefer another language, just mimic the same pattern:  
> • `GET https://.../domains/twitter.com`  
> • Add header `x-apikey`.

---

### 4️⃣ Typical Response Structure

A successful call returns something along these lines (truncated):

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "twitter.com",
    "links": { … },
    "relationships": { … },
    "type": "domains",
    "attributes": {
      "asn_owner": "Twitter Inc.",
      "country_code": "US",
      "first_seen": 1234567890,
      "last_analysis_stats": {
        "harmless": 100,
        "malicious": 5,
        "suspicious": 10,
        ...
      }
    }
  },
  "meta": {
    "pagination": { … }
  }
}
```

Key fields you might care about:

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `id` | The queried domain (`twitter.com`) |
| `attributes.asn_owner` | Owner of the IP range |
| `attributes.country_code` | ISO country code |
| `attributes.first_seen`, `last_seen` | Timestamps |
| `attributes.last_analysis_stats.*` | How many engines flagged it malicious/safe/etc. |

---

### 5️⃣ Rate Limits & Pagination

- Free tier → ~4 queries/minute.  
- Paid tiers allow higher limits.  
- Results may span multiple pages; check `"meta.pagination"` for links to next page.

---

### 6️⃣ Quick Checklist Before Running

1. Replace `twt_key_abc` with your real key (never expose publicly).  
2. Verify you’re allowed to hit `/domains/...`; some keys only support file scans.  
3. Handle errors gracefully (HTTP status codes ≥400).

---

That’s all! Once you run one of those snippets you’ll receive a full JSON payload describing everything VirusTotal knows about `twitter.com`. Happy scanning!
